entries:
Alpha 1.79.10 (forest floor and willow silhouettes)

  • Earth soil and forest litter have less obvious texture repetition. Moss detail is filtered at distance to reduce speckling while retaining the existing paths and ground-cover fields.
  • Mourning willows have curved hanging shoots and narrow leaves instead of reusing rounded birch foliage for their three curtains. All 256 leaves and existing High/Low triangle budgets, placements and walking clearances remain.
  • Fixed lighting on tilted woodland parts: their exact static transform is baked once so instanced normals remain correct. Geometry silhouettes, material ownership, shadows and quality switches are preserved; no additional tree parts or draw calls.
  • Raised-terrain preview rocks have narrower, varied shoulders and gentle fractures within their existing collision footprints. This is preview preparation: raised terrain remains disabled in ordinary public worlds. Wearable derivatives and broader renderer changes remain staged.
  • Future hosted browser installations have a 15-minute deadline, so stalled downloads fail visibly instead of blocking deployment for hours. All release test gates remain required.
  • Server, outage monitor, CI and isolated QA builds now use Go 1.27.2, fixing the newly reported reachable standard-library security issues. Dependency versions, vulnerability checks and deployment gates are unchanged.
  • Not the 1.80 feature freeze or full 1.87 modern-art completion. No account wipe, schema migration, quests, combat, economy or administrator-access changes. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.9 (woodland bark and natural undergrowth)

  • Earth-realm birch, pine and willow now have distinct bark: broken birch markings and peeling, coarse pine ridges and finer willow grain. Surface color, roughness and filtered relief follow the existing trunks instead of sharing generic timber.
  • Gloamwood grass and ferns form uneven stands with clearer gaps rather than a uniformly jittered grid. Every existing plant, species, scale and rotation is retained, with the same Low-quality subset. Roads, town approaches and investigation sites retain their walking clearances.
  • No new textures, lights or collision footprints. Tree placement, geometry, wind and shadows are unchanged. This is a woodland component improvement, not the 1.80 feature freeze or full 1.87 modern-art completion. Raised terrain, wearable derivatives and additional renderer optimizations remain staged.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, combat, quests, economy or administrator-access changes. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.8 (woodland foliage and cleaner UI startup)

  • Gloamwood pines have fuller hanging needle fans with varied height and stronger folds. Woodland sedge has curved, gently twisted leaves, varied blade widths and a greener palette instead of uniform flat ribbons.
  • The refinements retain every plant and tree, existing High/Low triangle counts, wind, lighting, shadows and collision footprints. Fuller pine fans stay inside the original crown-height envelope. They improve the existing code-owned woodland, not the whole-world composition or final modern-art milestone.
  • Published UI styles now load as one ordered stylesheet instead of forty separate requests. The same desktop and phone cascade, local fonts and startup recovery remain; source styles stay modular. This reduces startup requests, but does not guarantee recovery from every network failure.
  • This is not the 1.80 feature freeze or full 1.87 completion. Raised terrain, wearable derivatives and additional renderer optimizations remain staged. No account wipe, schema migration, gameplay, economy or administrator-access changes. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.7 (Earth surface refinement)

  • Gloamwood soil now has more coherent aggregate detail, with restrained damp-crevice and dry-face colors. Moss cushions use a separate broad field and retain sheltered woodland variation instead of blending every ground layer into one muddy wash.
  • The prepared rock material for staged raised terrain has bedding that is gently inclined and broken by weathering rather than embossed into contour-like lines. This does not activate the raised-world rocks. Existing geometry, collision footprints, roads, plants, lights and shadows remain unchanged; the refinement adds no meshes, textures or shader texture fetches.
  • This is a modest surface pass, not the 1.80 feature freeze or full 1.87 modern-art completion. Raised terrain and wearable derivatives remain staged, not enabled by this patch. Air-realm canvas was already delivered in 1.79.3 and is unchanged here.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, quest, economy, combat or administrator-access changes. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.6 (party healing hotbar input)

  • After selecting an ally in the party healing roster, numbered or remapped hotbar keys now work while the selected button retains keyboard focus. Healing Light and Divine Intervention keep the selected ally as their target; no extra world click is needed to regain gameplay input.
  • Only an enabled, selected healing-target button permits this shortcut. Typing fields, ordinary menu buttons, unselected or disabled roster buttons, modifier shortcuts and repeated key presses remain guarded. Enter and Space retain native button activation; focus remains accessible.
  • No changes to healing strength, range, mana cost, cooldowns, party credit or server authority. No account wipe, schema migration, economy or progression changes. Raised terrain and new wearable derivatives remain staged, not enabled by this patch. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.5 (administrator Dark Realm passage)

  • Verified administrators can enter the Dark Realm through the town Resonance Portal or Dungeon Guide without completing the crystal/story questline. Level 100, proximity and normal travel/action checks still apply. Ordinary players retain the existing story requirements.
  • Administrator passage does not complete quests or grant their rewards, and does not unlock the Umbral Nexus or Dark King raid quest gates. Valid saved Dark Realm positions are restored for administrators on login; access is checked against the current server-side account role, not a client flag.
  • The portal explains administrator passage without marking unrepaired crystals as restored. Permission use is audited and available under Dark Realm admin access in Administration activity history; role lookup or auditing failures do not grant privileged entry.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, economy or ordinary-player progression changes. Raised terrain remains disabled in production; full modern-art and release-readiness milestones remain open. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.4 (saved-position recovery and terrain compatibility)

  • Returning players are grounded at the current overworld floor when a flat-world save retains an elevated height. This prevents a character remaining suspended above town or the world after rejoining. Horizontal position, dungeon/casino floors, service offsets and active jump arcs remain owned by their existing systems.
  • The server now validates an explicit terrain profile before logs, journals, database work or player admission. Flat remains the default. The future raised-Earth profile loads hills and all 18 matching rock solids together; selecting terrain never grants QA commands. Unknown or incomplete profiles are refused instead of silently changing the world.
  • Focused compatibility checks cover four classes and 16 fresh saved sessions through flat, raised, flat and raised configurations, retaining equipment, bag/stash/buyback items, HP/MP, Gold/EP, quests and progression. A connected Wizard check covers raised walking, actual Fireball draws and damage, and matching-profile reconnect. These are prepared disposable fixtures, not whole-campaign balance or physical-phone acceptance.
  • Raised terrain remains disabled in production. This compatibility precursor is not the 1.80 freeze or full 1.87 art/performance milestone; equipped-party performance, final modern art and remaining launch gates still require their own evidence.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, damage tuning, reward change, payment integration, public-access change or alert-setting change. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.3 (town masonry, elemental landscapes and dungeon architecture)

  • Lanternhold buildings, courtyard walls and street furniture gain weathered masonry with quieter mortar and coordinated surface detail. Building placement, walking space and collisions remain unchanged.
  • Fire ground gains folded basalt and ash; Moonfrost gains softer weathered ice and rime, with beveled Tide Rib pier courses and attached tide marks. Stormcrown Reach gains wind-worn slate and gently billowed camp canvas. These are loading-time details, not per-frame cloth simulation.
  • Molten Core, Tempest Spire, Abyssal Well and Umbral Nexus gain coordinated color, relief and roughness and distinctive blind arcades, piers and trim. Blind arcades are decorative, not new passages. Existing wall bounds, floors, layouts, collision boxes, entrances and progression remain unchanged; transparent camera cutaway walls stay simple and readable. Verdant retains its established surfaces.
  • Elemental dungeon textures respect High/Low quality. Changing quality while inside an affected dungeon offers a reload instead of rebuilding the instance or resetting its progress. Existing texture counts remain unchanged; detailed walls and canvas add bounded geometry.
  • Desktop and phone-sized rendered checks cover equipped characters and the real HUD at ordinary gameplay zoom. This is a scoped visual patch, not the 1.80 feature freeze, full 1.87 art milestone, final modern-art approval, physical-phone party test or whole-game performance guarantee. Raised terrain remains disabled in production.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, balance, Gold/EP, equipment restriction, character animation, access, payment or alert-setting change. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.2 (woodland rendering, Moonfrost surfaces and release trust)

  • Woodland crowns and ground cover use more selective render batches while retaining every tree, leaf and plant, their original detail and unchanged collisions. Static bounds reuse creation-time vertex work; no extra per-frame vertex scan. High woodland reference now measures 249,406 triangles and 338 draw calls within the original limits. All three High and Low reference views pass; this is not a whole-world or every-device performance guarantee.
  • Gloamwood leaves gain subtle veins and shadow-aware light wrapping. Rock materials use registered mineral detail across differently angled faces, and optional raised-world outcrops retain sharp cleaves with smoother weathered shoulders. Silhouettes and collision geometry stay unchanged.
  • Moonfrost ground gains weathered ice sheets, wind-deposited rime and short broken fissures with matching color, relief and roughness on High and Low. The existing texture count, geometry and gameplay stay unchanged.
  • The renderer respects saved graphics quality from startup; Low-quality startup no longer briefly creates High-quality postprocessing. Ground-anchored, snapped shadow coverage and conservative foliage shadow bounds preserve off-screen shadows, restoring temporary flags after normal rendering, errors and disposal.
  • Deployment uses a pinned public host key, strict verification and bounded SSH waits. Native QA runs only from trusted production branches and the canonical repository; ordinary hosted checks retain separate queues. This does not repair external SSH routing or bypass deployment guards.
  • This is a scoped rendering/release-trust patch, not the 1.80 feature freeze or the full 1.87 art milestone. Raised-Earth live integration, final modern-art/equipped-party review, human pacing and supported-device acceptance remain open.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, balance, Gold/EP, equipment restriction, animation, access, payment or alert-setting change. Full prior patch history remains below.

Alpha 1.79.1 (realm-ground polish and stricter browser origins)

  • Gloamwood ground gains clearer soil and moss layering, warmer fallen leaves and coordinated shallow relief and roughness. Registered fields stay in place across High and Low quality; no additional textures or draw calls, terrain displacement or collision changes.
  • Stormcrown's ground gains broken wind-worn slate layers and pale scree deposits, with matching color, shallow relief and roughness on High and Low. Existing terrain textures and geometry stay the same; the added geological fields are generated during loading, not each frame.
  • Browser WebSocket admission rejects malformed Origin URLs, invalid ports, blank or duplicate Origin headers. Existing trusted domains and local development ports remain; native clients without an Origin still require normal authentication.
  • Failed equipment-model binding releases partially prepared owned parts without changing cached assets or previously equipped gear and body coverage. Older failed loading requests cannot clear a newer equipment request's visual status; successful item fit and animations remain unchanged.
  • Deployment checks free space on the checkout and actual Docker storage filesystems before cleanup, image builds or service replacement. The default 2 GiB minimum refuses low or unknown storage without automatic deletion; it is not a guarantee of peak build or backup capacity.
  • This is a scoped polish/security patch, not the 1.80 feature freeze. Raised-Earth production delivery, the remaining High woodland performance limit and final modern-art review remain open; the unfinished future terrain/performance branch is not included.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, balance, Gold/EP, equipment restrictions, animation, access or alert-setting change. Full prior patch history remains below.
